Fit a hidden Markov step selection model

Source: R/fit.R
fit_ssf.Rd

Uses either the published SSF importance approximation or exact canonical kernel normalisation, with the HMM forward algorithm, through either a compiled analytic-gradient engine or an independent R reference. All fitted SSF and transition parameters are passed from the best short run to the long run. Errors and warnings are retained for every attempt. This implementation prioritises verifiability, with cross-checks between the two engines.

Usage

fit_ssf(
  data,
  formula = ~step + log_step + cos_angle,
  n_states = 2L,
  n_starts = 5L,
  short_iter = 30L,
  long_iter = 300L,
  spread = 0.5,
  seed = NULL,
  engine = c("native", "R"),
  initial_values = NULL,
  normalization = c("importance", "exact"),
  transition_hour = NULL,
  transition_harmonics = 2L,
  step_harmonics = 0L
)

Arguments

data

Case-control data accepted by prepare_ssf_data(), or observed prepare_ssf_steps() data when normalization is exact.

formula

One-sided SSF formula. For exact fitting, add lag_log_step to estimate a state-specific AR(1) coefficient for the log gamma mean. The previous length is used within a segment, including across state changes. Add any of lag22_log_step through lag26_log_step with lag_log_step and transition_hour to include those hourly lags. A lag only contributes when its step is available in the same segment. The absolute lag coefficients sum to less than one in each state.

n_states

Number of hidden states, between 1 and 6.

n_starts

Number of short runs. A one-state model uses one run.

short_iter, long_iter

Maximum BFGS iterations for short and long phases.

spread

Positive standard deviation of initial perturbations. A scalar or named vector with one entry for each SSF design column.

seed

Optional integer seed, restored to the previous RNG state on exit.

engine

"native" uses the compiled objective and analytic gradient; "R" uses the independent R objective with numerical derivatives.

initial_values

Optional list with a coefficient matrix and positive transition matrix, named coefficients and transition. Included as the first short-run start; remaining starts are random perturbations. For daily transitions, supply transition_coefficients from a previous fit with the same transition harmonics in place of transition. Supply step_hour_coefficients from a fit with the same length harmonics to reuse those effects. They start at zero by default.

normalization

importance uses case-control data; exact requires observed data from prepare_ssf_steps() and supports only the canonical gamma-von Mises terms and optional prospective target direction. Exact fitting optimises log rate and log shape to preserve positive gamma parameters. AR coefficients use a hyperbolic tangent link. Spread applies on the working scale. Reported coefficients, covariance and score are on the natural coefficient scale.

transition_hour

Optional integer hour (0 to 23) at the beginning of each step. Daily transitions require two states and exact fitting on hourly observations. Supply hours in a consistent time zone.

transition_harmonics

Number of sine/cosine pairs, from 1 to 5, when transition_hour is supplied. Each switch direction has its own logit regression. Each segment starts in the periodic stationary distribution for its initial hour.

step_harmonics

Number of sine/cosine pairs in the log mean of the gamma step length, from 0 to 5. A positive value requires transition_hour. Each state has its own curve. The curve adds to the log mean after any AR(1) adjustment. The gamma shape remains fixed within each state.

Value

An ssf_fit object containing coefficients, transition matrix, log likelihood, covariance when the Hessian is positive definite, decoded states, smoothed probabilities, diagnostics, and the full start log. With daily transitions, transition is a 2 by 2 by 24 array indexed by step-origin hour. transition_coefficients contains the two switching regressions and initial gives state probabilities by hour. If step_harmonics is positive, step_hour_coefficients holds the hourly log-mean coefficients, one column per state. The movement coefficients describe the baseline before the hourly adjustment. Use decode_ssf_diel() to score new observations. After BFGS converges, a local Newton correction can reduce the score when the Hessian is positive definite. It accepts a correction when the largest absolute score falls and the objective improves or agrees to rounding precision. The Hessian is recomputed at the retained solution. The score_refinement diagnostic records the largest absolute score before this step and the number of accepted corrections. The convergence code and the original BFGS logs retain their optimiser meaning. For exact fits the stored Hessian uses working log-rate/log-shape parameters; covariance and score use the reported natural coefficient scale.
